scenes.headline: How Leviathan answers an agent without reading the data
scenes.sub: One SQLite file, a ranked search, and five short cards.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jalebi! Leviathan lets an agent ask about a huge table without reading it. Here's how it works.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Search inside one entity's history with a full-text index, and hand the agent five capped, cited cards instead of raw rows.
scenes.say: Search inside one customer's or machine's history with a full-text index. Then hand the agent five short cards, not raw rows.

steps.say: First it resolves the machine you named: exact key, then name, then a fuzzy match. If two match, it asks instead of guessing.
Every record carries a hidden token for its machine, so the search only touches that machine's records.
Your words are ranked with BM25, then nudged up for records that say what was actually done.
The best five become cards, and each card's id is a citation the agent can fetch in full.

scenes.title: How a record becomes a card
scenes.say: Here's what goes on a card.

items.say: The id, the date and the rank.
A few chosen fields, each cut short.
And the one sentence that best matches your words.

left.title: Grep the history
items: Output grows with the machine's records
left.say: Grep prints everything about the machine, so its output grows with the history.

right.title: Five capped cards
items: Every field has a character cap
right.say: Leviathan prints five capped cards, so its answer can't grow, however big the table gets.

steps.say: On the project's own synthetic log of a million records, the median answer is a few hundred tokens. The better grep is over a hundred thousand.

scenes.label: relevant records behind every benchmark question
scenes.say: One caveat. Every benchmark question has at least four right answers, and the questions share most words with the records. So the ninety-nine percent is a friendly test.

scenes.text: The small answer is a design choice: rank inside one entity, then cap what each record can say.
scenes.say: The small answer is a design choice. Rank inside one entity, then cap what each record can say.
